sentences.span: BofA's explanation is that in a market with "a relatively fixed supply of attention"... AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying, which the bank calls simply the "AI put."
sentences.why: BofA (source field confirms bank) coins and names the concept exactly as the sentence states.

sentences.span: macro risk "is struggling to compete for attention with the growth potential of AI narratives." AI FOMO drives aggressive dip-buying, which the bank calls simply the "AI put."
sentences.why: Fixed attention supply, AI narratives winning attention from macro risk, and dip-buying mechanism are all stated directly; the bracket citation markers are not evidence but the underlying claim is fully supported.

sentences.span: Have higher rates been a constraint on the stock market of late? For sure... Now, for the bears... Now, for the bulls...
sentences.why: Pasquariello (Goldman hedge-fund coverage desk) lays out a bear case (Ben Snider / 2-sigma rule) and a bull case (Privorotsky / 1999 analog, Goldman one-delta/EMEA cash desk) on what the bond-market move means for stocks — a genuine split between two Goldman desks.

sentences.span: one year ago, the forward P/E of S&P was 23x; today it's 19x... S&P has been mired in a tyrannical range trade around the 7700 level for the past two months.
sentences.why: Both the multiple compression (23x to 19x) and the ~7700 range are stated verbatim.

sentences.span: The recent rapid rise in yields has triggered a number of historical-data backed red flags (it's the velocity, not the level)...
sentences.why: Matches almost verbatim; the companion Pasquariello note (18561) independently corroborates with its 'speed limit' / 2-standard-deviation framing.

sentences.span: His checklist for getting more constructive is refreshingly simple: "I need rates to calm, credit to stop widening and a more definitive energy solution before taking nets up here."
sentences.why: The three-item checklist (rates, credit, energy) and the attribution to Privorotsky match exactly; 'taking nets up' is desk shorthand for adding equity risk.

sentences.span: France, with its deteriorating fiscal trajectory, could be the first sign of the cracks.
sentences.why: Directly supports the framing that France is where the global rates move is breaking something.

sentences.span: Fair value for the 10y OAT-Bund spread stands at 100-110bp... We cut our French growth forecasts again, to 0.3% and 0.6% for this year and next
sentences.why: Both figures (spread fair value and growth forecast cuts) match exactly, attributed to BofA Global Research.

sentences.span: The bigger question is structural: can Europe sustain US-driven higher global rates when growth is running at just ~1%?
sentences.why: Matches the sentence's framing of the open question; the paragraph is explicitly tagged "GS" in the source.

sentences.span: 2026 projected hyperscaler issuance of $250bn... most of this year's funding ($230bn) completed... now expecting $420bn of global direct IG issuance from the cohort (vs. $400bn previously)... 35% of 2027's hyperscaler CapEx spending will be debt funded
sentences.why: Every figure (current-year total, amount done, revised 2027 forecast and prior forecast, debt-funded share) is stated verbatim by Goldman's credit strategists.

sentences.span: The junkiest junk is leading credit losses but the rest of high yield is starting to catch up.
sentences.why: Directly supports the framing that stress is concentrated at the bottom of the credit stack.

sentences.span: CCCs hit 1,007 bps, the first time above 1,000 since the March 2023 bank scare... Oracle matters here purely as a credit story. Its 5Y CDS hit a record ~227 bps, its 2056 bonds yield above 8%
sentences.why: Both the CCC-spread figure/comparison and the Oracle CDS/bond-yield figures are stated verbatim in the same source.

sentences.span: I should also note here that the "speed limit" is most acute when it's driven by a surge in real yields.
sentences.why: Pasquariello's bear case and Privorotsky's note (18559: "Real rates are very high", framed as the structural driver of the stress) both center the equity-risk trigger on real yields, supporting the 'both sides name the same trigger' framing.

sentences.span: Oil prices extended the week's rise, with Brent above $102 by late Friday
sentences.why: Price figure matches exactly; the Persian Gulf export figure (23.6mb/d, just above 2025 average) and 'roughly balanced' market framing are independently confirmed in 18660 (Daan Struyven, Goldman): 'recovered to 23.6mb/d over the last week or just above their 2025 average... global oil market appears roughly balanced.'

sentences.span: our base case that Brent prices moderate to $85/bbl by year-end and to $80 in 2027
sentences.why: Goldman's Brent forecast matches exactly; the G7 100-million-barrel release is independently confirmed in 18672: 'G7 nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of' oil and diesel.
